graph_metadata.assignment_objective: Implement and analyse autocomplete as a tree-search problem using individual-word prefix-tree construction, BFS, DFS, and UCS with frequency-based costs.
design_notes: Teacher KC IDs and source wording are preserved as the authoritative layer.
Derived sub-KCs use a separate SKC namespace and are reusable across multiple teacher KCs to avoid duplication.
Source-stated edges and inferred edges are distinguished by provenance and confidence.
Task IDs remain node attributes rather than graph nodes to keep the KC graph compact.
Symmetric commonly-confused relations are stored once in canonical order.
Only high-value inferred cross-KC links are included to reduce graph density and preserve interpretability.

relation_semantics.parent_of: Hierarchical decomposition: target is a more specific component of source.
relation_semantics.prerequisite_of: Source should normally be mastered before target.
relation_semantics.supports: Source provides useful knowledge/evidence for target but is not treated as strictly required.
relation_semantics.related_to: Conceptually related without a stronger directional claim.
relation_semantics.commonly_confused_with: Symmetric diagnostic relation indicating concepts students may conflate.

nodes.name: Modelling autocomplete as tree search
nodes.definition: Understanding autocomplete as search over a character tree where prefixes define where search begins and completions are found by traversing paths.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains autocomplete as searching a tree from a prefix to completed entries.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Is autocomplete just matching strings, or is it really a search problem? | interpretation: Student may not understand the search-problem framing. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Identifying the prefix endpoint as the autocomplete search start state
nodes.definition: Determining that search begins at the node reached after following all characters of the typed prefix.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Starts BFS, DFS, and UCS from the prefix endpoint node.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: Should BFS start from the root or from the last letter of the prefix? | interpretation: Student may be unsure how the prefix defines the search start state. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Recognizing completed entries as autocomplete goal states
nodes.definition: Understanding that a valid word ending is a goal state in autocomplete search.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Distinguishes complete words from intermediate prefix nodes.
nodes.difficulty_signals: misconception: Every leaf node is a word, so I do not need to mark word endings. | interpretation: Student may confuse leaf nodes with completed entries. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Representing suggestions as paths through a character tree
nodes.definition: Understanding that a suggestion is formed by concatenating characters along a path in the tree.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains that full suggestions come from complete character paths.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: My function only returns the last character, not the full word. | interpretation: Student may not connect paths to full suggestions. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Treating autocomplete as a multiple-goal search problem
nodes.definition: Continuing search to collect multiple valid completions rather than stopping after the first one.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Does not stop after the first valid completion.
nodes.difficulty_signals: misconception: Once I find the first word, can I return immediately? | interpretation: Student may not recognize autocomplete as multiple-goal search. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Representing and constructing autocomplete prefix trees
nodes.definition: Understanding and building the character-based prefix tree used for autocomplete entries.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains the role of the prefix tree in storing and retrieving autocomplete entries.
nodes.difficulty_signals: information_seeking: What exactly is a prefix tree in this assignment? | interpretation: Student is seeking the tree-construction model. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Representing words in a prefix tree
nodes.definition: Understanding how individual words are stored by sharing common prefixes and branching at differing characters.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly explains shared-prefix branching.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Do I create a separate branch for every word even if they start the same? | interpretation: Student may not understand shared-prefix representation. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Parsing the document into individual autocomplete words
nodes.definition: Splitting the input document into individual words that can be inserted into the autocomplete prefix tree.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Extracts individual words from the document before character insertion.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: Should I insert the whole document as one string or split it first? | interpretation: Student may not understand the word-parsing step before tree insertion. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Constructing a prefix tree by inserting character paths
nodes.definition: Inserting each word into the tree character by character, creating child nodes only when needed.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly creates or reuses child nodes while inserting words.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: How do I insert each character into the children dictionary? | interpretation: Student likely needs help with procedural tree insertion. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Designing terminal-state representation for completed entries
nodes.definition: Implementing a way to mark or recognize that a node corresponds to a completed word.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly detects complete words even when they have children.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: How will I know that the is complete if it also has children? | interpretation: Student recognizes the terminal-state issue but may not know how to implement it. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Choosing a duplicate-entry handling strategy
nodes.definition: Deciding how repeated words affect suggestions, frequency counts, and output duplication.
nodes.student_must_know_do: States whether duplicates affect output, frequency, or both.
nodes.difficulty_signals: uncertainty: Should duplicate words appear twice in suggestions or just increase frequency? | interpretation: Student is identifying an intentional design choice. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Tracing and visualizing prefix-tree construction
nodes.definition: Manually tracing inserted words and producing a tree diagram showing shared prefixes and branches.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Produces a correct diagram with shared prefixes and branches.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: I cannot draw the tree from test.txt; I do not know where branches split. | interpretation: Student may struggle to trace prefix sharing manually. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Locating and validating the prefix endpoint before search
nodes.definition: Traversing the tree according to a prefix and handling absent or empty prefixes safely before running search.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Suggestions are generated only from the prefix subtree.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: My suggestions do not begin with the prefix. | interpretation: Prefix endpoint lookup may be wrong. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Distinguishing autocomplete search strategies
nodes.definition: Understanding how BFS, DFS, and UCS differ in frontier policy, expansion order, and output behaviour.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains how BFS, DFS, and UCS differ.
nodes.difficulty_signals: information_seeking: What is the real difference between BFS, DFS, and UCS here? | interpretation: Student is asking about algorithm-strategy distinctions. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Selecting the correct frontier policy for BFS, DFS, and UCS
nodes.definition: Choosing FIFO queue behaviour for BFS, LIFO/recursion behaviour for DFS, and priority-based behaviour for UCS.
aliases: queue vs stack vs priority queue
nodes.student_must_know_do: Matches each algorithm to its correct frontier policy.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Can I use a queue for all three algorithms? | interpretation: Student may not distinguish FIFO, LIFO, and priority frontier policies. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Explaining breadth-first autocomplete ordering
nodes.definition: Explaining why BFS explores level by level and tends to return shorter completions earlier.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly describes BFS ordering and same-depth tie dependence on child order.
nodes.difficulty_signals: misconception: BFS gives the most frequent words first. | interpretation: Student confuses BFS ordering with frequency or UCS ordering. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Explaining depth-first autocomplete traversal
nodes.definition: Explaining why DFS follows one branch deeply before backtracking to alternatives.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly describes depth-first traversal and backtracking.
nodes.difficulty_signals: misconception: DFS checks all short words first before long words. | interpretation: Student may confuse DFS with BFS. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Explaining UCS as lowest-cumulative-cost expansion
nodes.definition: Explaining that UCS expands the path with the lowest accumulated cost first.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Distinguishes UCS from BFS and DFS using cumulative cost.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Why does UCS need costs? Is it just another DFS? | interpretation: Student may not understand cost-prioritized expansion. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Comparing traversal-order differences among BFS, DFS, and UCS
nodes.definition: Comparing how BFS, DFS, and UCS produce different suggestion orders from the same prefix.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains output differences using algorithm behaviour.
nodes.difficulty_signals: output_interpretation: The algorithms return the same words, so are they basically the same? | interpretation: Student may not attend to traversal-order differences. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Interpreting informal suggestion quality differences across algorithms
nodes.definition: Interpreting whether different algorithm outputs appear more useful or natural without using a formal metric.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Gives justified informal comparison of suggestion usefulness.
nodes.difficulty_signals: advanced_inquiry: Can I justify quality by saying UCS favours common transitions? | interpretation: Student is reasoning about informal suggestion quality. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Implementing autocomplete search algorithms
nodes.definition: Implementing BFS, DFS, and UCS traversal logic to generate autocomplete suggestions from the prefix subtree.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Produces working autocomplete search methods.
nodes.difficulty_signals: insufficient_evidence: Can you implement the search algorithms for me? | interpretation: Student may be answer-seeking, but the exact weak KC is unclear. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Implementing BFS autocomplete with a FIFO frontier
nodes.definition: Implementing BFS using a first-in, first-out frontier while tracking paths and collecting completed suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Returns BFS-ordered suggestions as a list.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: My BFS works like DFS because it goes deep into one branch. | interpretation: Student may be using the wrong frontier operation or queue discipline. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Implementing recursive DFS autocomplete
nodes.definition: Implementing DFS using recursive calls to explore child paths and collect completed suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Can implement or reason about recursive DFS as a DFS option.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: My recursive DFS never stops or gives recursion errors. | interpretation: Student may struggle with recursive DFS base cases or traversal structure. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Implementing stack-based DFS autocomplete
nodes.definition: Implementing DFS using an explicit stack to explore child paths and collect completed suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Can implement or reason about stack-based DFS as a DFS option.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: My stack DFS gives the reverse order from what I expected. | interpretation: Student may not understand stack push/pop order. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Comparing recursive DFS with stack-based DFS
nodes.definition: Explaining how recursive DFS and stack-based DFS differ in control flow, state storage, and possible output order.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Clearly compares recursive and stack-based DFS and can justify a choice.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Recursive DFS and stack DFS are completely different algorithms, right? | interpretation: Student may not understand that both implement DFS with different state storage. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Choosing child traversal order for deterministic suggestions
nodes.definition: Selecting and consistently applying an order for visiting child nodes so suggestion order is explainable.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Uses a consistent child traversal order and can explain its effect on results.
nodes.difficulty_signals: uncertainty: Should I sort children alphabetically or use insertion order? | interpretation: Student is dealing with traversal-order design. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Maintaining search-path state to reconstruct complete suggestions
nodes.definition: Carrying enough path information during traversal to return the full word, not only a suffix or node value.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Returns full suggestion strings from BFS, DFS, and UCS.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: I found the correct node, but I only return the suffix after the prefix. | interpretation: Student may not maintain complete path state during traversal. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Continuing search after finding one completion
nodes.definition: Ensuring the algorithm keeps exploring after the first valid completion so all relevant suggestions can be returned.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Collects multiple completions rather than returning the first match only.
nodes.difficulty_signals: debugging_difficulty: Only one suggestion appears even though there should be many. | interpretation: Student may stop search after the first terminal state. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Implementing UCS cost and priority-queue logic
nodes.definition: Implementing the frequency, cost, and priority-queue logic needed for UCS autocomplete suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Cost and priority logic supports UCS ordering.
nodes.difficulty_signals: information_seeking: What data do I need to store for UCS costs? | interpretation: Student is asking about UCS cost modelling broadly. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Storing transition-frequency information for UCS
nodes.definition: Recording how often character transitions occur so UCS costs can be calculated.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Stores transition counts needed for inverse-frequency cost calculation.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: Where should I count how often each transition appears? | interpretation: Student may not know how to store frequency information during tree construction. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Selecting a UCS transition-frequency model
nodes.definition: Choosing whether UCS transition frequencies are based on immediate previous character context or full-prefix context.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Chooses and explains one frequency model consistently.
nodes.difficulty_signals: uncertainty: Should the frequency be based on the previous character or the whole prefix? | interpretation: Student is identifying an allowed modelling choice. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Calculating inverse-frequency transition costs
nodes.definition: Converting transition frequency into cost so more frequent transitions receive lower costs.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly converts transition frequencies into costs.
nodes.difficulty_signals: mathematical_calculation: If a transition appears 5 times, what should its cost be? | interpretation: Student may need help converting frequency into inverse cost. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Accumulating path costs across character transitions
nodes.definition: Computing cumulative UCS path cost by adding transition costs along a candidate suggestion path.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Uses cumulative path cost to prioritize UCS frontier entries.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Do I compare only the next letter cost or the total path cost? | interpretation: Student may confuse transition cost with cumulative path cost. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Implementing UCS autocomplete with a priority queue
nodes.definition: Implementing UCS with a priority queue or heap that expands the lowest-cost path and handles equal-cost entries safely.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Returns UCS-ordered suggestions using accumulated costs.
nodes.difficulty_signals: debugging_difficulty: heapq gives an error when two costs are the same. | interpretation: Student is facing priority-queue tie-handling or tuple-comparison issues. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Verifying and interpreting autocomplete outputs
nodes.definition: Checking generated autocomplete outputs and using them to reason about algorithm behaviour.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Uses outputs as evidence for correctness and comparison.
nodes.difficulty_signals: insufficient_evidence: Is my output correct? | interpretation: Student requests verification, but the weak KC is unclear without output or code. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Interpreting and preserving algorithm-specific suggestion order
nodes.definition: Recording suggestions in the exact order produced by the algorithm and interpreting that order correctly.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Does not sort or reorder output lists before reporting.
nodes.difficulty_signals: verification_request: Should I sort the suggestions before writing them in the report? | interpretation: Student may not understand algorithm-specific order preservation. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Verifying autocomplete behaviour with controlled prefixes and corpora
nodes.definition: Testing with controlled prefixes or small corpora to check whether tree construction and search behaviour are plausible.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Uses test.txt, required prefix th, and additional prefixes to check behaviour.
nodes.difficulty_signals: verification_request: Can I test with test.txt first before genZ.txt? | interpretation: Student is seeking a controlled testing strategy. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Comparing generated suggestion lists across algorithms
nodes.definition: Using BFS, DFS, and UCS output lists as evidence to compare algorithm behaviour.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Compares generated lists using algorithm behaviour rather than arbitrary preference.
nodes.difficulty_signals: output_interpretation: BFS and DFS have different lists; how do I explain the difference? | interpretation: Student needs help interpreting generated outputs across algorithms. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Diagnosing autocomplete implementation errors
nodes.definition: Identifying and reasoning about faults in tree construction, traversal, cost handling, or output generation.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Narrows vague failure symptoms to likely implementation causes.
nodes.difficulty_signals: insufficient_evidence: My code is not working. | interpretation: Student signals debugging need, but the relevant KC is unknown. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Diagnosing missing autocomplete suggestions
nodes.definition: Identifying why expected suggestions are absent, such as insertion errors, terminal-marker errors, or prefix-lookup errors.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Checks tree insertion, terminal markers, and prefix lookup when expected words are missing.
nodes.difficulty_signals: debugging_difficulty: The word is in the file, but it never appears as a suggestion. | interpretation: Missing suggestion may result from insertion, terminal marking, or prefix lookup. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Diagnosing incorrect suggestion order
nodes.definition: Identifying why suggestions appear in an unexpected order due to frontier use, child traversal order, or output sorting.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Checks frontier policy, child traversal order, and accidental sorting.
nodes.difficulty_signals: debugging_difficulty: I get the right suggestions but the wrong order. | interpretation: Student likely needs help with frontier policy, child traversal, or sorting mistakes. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Diagnosing priority-queue ordering or tie-breaking errors
nodes.definition: Identifying UCS errors caused by incorrect priority values, equal-cost handling, or unsafe heap entries.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Recognizes and fixes priority-queue ordering or tie-handling problems.
nodes.difficulty_signals: debugging_difficulty: UCS gives random-looking results even though I calculated frequencies. | interpretation: Student may have incorrect priority values, cumulative cost, or tie handling. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Diagnosing premature stopping after one completion
nodes.definition: Identifying when a search implementation incorrectly returns after the first completion instead of collecting multiple suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Finds and fixes early-return behaviour in search methods.
nodes.difficulty_signals: debugging_difficulty: My search returns after the first match; how do I get all matches? | interpretation: Strong evidence of premature stopping issue. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Explaining implementation logic for tree construction and search
nodes.definition: Explaining the reasoning and control flow behind submitted tree-construction and search implementations.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Gives clear code-intuition explanations grounded in the submitted code.
nodes.difficulty_signals: insufficient_evidence: Can you write the explanation section? | interpretation: Student may be seeking wording, but mastery cannot be inferred. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Explaining prefix-tree construction logic
nodes.definition: Explaining how the implementation parses words, inserts characters, reuses shared prefixes, and marks completed entries.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains word parsing, character insertion, prefix reuse, and terminal marking.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: How do I explain build_tree without just saying it loops? | interpretation: Student may struggle to articulate prefix-tree construction logic. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Explaining BFS implementation logic
nodes.definition: Explaining how the BFS implementation uses a FIFO frontier, tracks paths, and collects suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains FIFO queue use, path tracking, and terminal collection.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: How do I explain why my BFS uses a queue? | interpretation: Student may understand code but not connect it to BFS logic. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Explaining DFS implementation logic
nodes.definition: Explaining how the DFS implementation explores branches, uses recursion or a stack, and collects suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains DFS implementation style and its traversal behaviour.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: How do I explain recursive DFS versus stack DFS? | interpretation: Student may not distinguish the two DFS implementation styles. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Explaining UCS implementation logic
nodes.definition: Explaining how the UCS implementation uses frequency-derived costs and a priority queue to order suggestions.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Explains frequency counting, inverse costs, cumulative costs, and priority queue ordering.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: How should I explain UCS cost in my code? | interpretation: Student may need help connecting frequency, cost, heap ordering, and output. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Explaining implementation assumptions clearly
nodes.definition: Stating and justifying choices about duplicates, UCS frequency model, child traversal order, tie-breaking, and optional text handling.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Clearly documents design assumptions and applies them consistently.
nodes.difficulty_signals: repeated_clarification: Student repeatedly asks whether duplicates, cost model, or tie-breaking must match one official answer. | interpretation: Student may not understand that some choices are assumptions to state clearly. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Integrating implemented suggestion methods into the starter application
nodes.definition: Connecting completed BFS, DFS, or UCS methods to the provided application flow so the GUI or main program uses the intended algorithm.
nodes.student_must_know_do: GUI or direct execution uses the intended implemented algorithm.
nodes.difficulty_signals: implementation_difficulty: I implemented BFS but the GUI still shows random suggestions. | interpretation: Student likely did not connect the implemented method to the active suggestion function. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Applying consistent implementation assumptions
nodes.definition: Applying chosen assumptions consistently across parsing, duplicates, cost calculation, traversal order, and reporting.
nodes.student_must_know_do: No contradictions appear across duplicate handling, frequency model, traversal order, and reporting.
nodes.difficulty_signals: procedural_difficulty: I used duplicates for UCS frequency but removed them from output; is that inconsistent? | interpretation: Student may need to apply assumptions consistently across parts. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Iterating over characters in Python strings
nodes.definition: Using Python string iteration to process each character in a word.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Correctly loops over characters in each parsed word.
nodes.difficulty_signals: prerequisite_knowledge: How do I loop through each character in a string? | interpretation: Student may lack Python string iteration prerequisite. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Using Python dictionaries for membership and lookup
nodes.definition: Checking whether keys exist in dictionaries and retrieving or assigning values for child-node mappings.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Uses child dictionary membership checks and assignments correctly.
nodes.difficulty_signals: prerequisite_knowledge: How do I check if a key exists in a dictionary? | interpretation: Student may lack dictionary lookup prerequisite needed for child nodes. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Accessing and updating Python object attributes
nodes.definition: Reading and modifying object attributes in class instances, including starter and added node metadata.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Adds and uses node metadata correctly.
nodes.difficulty_signals: prerequisite_knowledge: How do I add a new attribute like is_word to a Node? | interpretation: Student may lack object-attribute knowledge. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Building and returning Python lists of results
nodes.definition: Accumulating suggestion strings in a list and returning that list from a function.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Returns a list of suggestions rather than printing only or returning None.
nodes.difficulty_signals: prerequisite_knowledge: My function prints suggestions but returns None. | interpretation: Student may not understand returning a list of results. | sufficient_alone=True

nodes.name: Controlling traversal loops over a frontier
nodes.definition: Using loop conditions to repeatedly process queue, stack, or heap frontiers until traversal is complete.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Uses correct while-frontier loop behaviour in BFS, stack DFS, and UCS.
nodes.difficulty_signals: prerequisite_knowledge: Why do we use while queue instead of one for loop? | interpretation: Student may not understand frontier-loop control. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Distinguishing tree search from graph search
nodes.definition: Understanding that a prefix tree has tree-like traversal properties and usually differs from general graph search with repeated-state cycles.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Does not overapply graph visited-set logic when traversing a prefix tree.
nodes.difficulty_signals: conceptual_confusion: Do I need a visited set like graph search? | interpretation: Student may be mixing tree search and graph search. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Choosing text normalization rules
nodes.definition: Deciding whether and how to normalize text, such as case handling, before inserting words or comparing prefixes.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Applies normalization choice consistently if used.
nodes.difficulty_signals: advanced_inquiry: Should I lowercase all entries before building the tree? | interpretation: Student is considering optional text normalization. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Handling punctuation and special characters as tree characters
nodes.definition: Deciding whether punctuation or non-letter symbols should be inserted and searched as valid characters in the autocomplete tree.
nodes.student_must_know_do: Handles symbols consistently if they appear in the corpus.
nodes.difficulty_signals: advanced_inquiry: Should punctuation be treated like a normal character in the tree? | interpretation: Student is considering optional special-character handling. | sufficient_alone=False

nodes.name: Identifying states, actions, and goals in a search problem
nodes.definition: Distinguishing the current state, possible transitions/actions, and goal test when formulating a problem as search.

nodes.name: Using rooted-tree vocabulary
nodes.definition: Recognizing roots, nodes, child edges, paths, branches, and depth in a rooted tree.

nodes.name: Recognizing the string-prefix relation
nodes.definition: Determining whether one string is the starting substring (prefix) of another string.

nodes.name: Distinguishing terminal nodes from leaf nodes
nodes.definition: Understanding that a completed word can end at a node that still has children, so terminal status is not the same as being a leaf.

nodes.name: Collecting multiple goals instead of stopping at the first
nodes.definition: Understanding that a search can continue after finding one goal in order to collect additional valid goal states.

nodes.name: Splitting input text into word tokens
nodes.definition: Using a consistent tokenization rule, such as whitespace splitting, to turn a document into individual candidate words.

nodes.name: Iterating over a collection of words
nodes.definition: Using a loop to process each parsed word one at a time.

nodes.name: Understanding Python string iteration behavior
nodes.definition: Knowing that iterating over a Python string yields its characters in sequence, one character value per iteration.

nodes.name: Checking whether a Python dictionary key exists
nodes.definition: Using membership testing such as `key in dictionary` before lookup or insertion.

nodes.name: Retrieving a Python dictionary value by key
nodes.definition: Accessing the value associated with an existing dictionary key.

nodes.name: Adding or updating a Python dictionary entry
nodes.definition: Assigning a value to a dictionary key to create or update a mapping.

nodes.name: Applying create-or-reuse logic for child nodes
nodes.definition: Creating a new child only when a character key is absent and otherwise reusing the existing child node.

nodes.name: Using dot notation to read and assign instance fields
nodes.definition: Using expressions such as `node.is_word` and assignments such as `node.is_word = True` to access instance state.

nodes.name: Using a Boolean terminal flag
nodes.definition: Representing completed-word status with a Boolean attribute and testing that flag during search.

nodes.name: Tracing shared-prefix branching
nodes.definition: Recognizing where inserted words share the same path and where they diverge into separate child branches.

nodes.name: Following a prefix path from the root
nodes.definition: Traversing child mappings character by character to reach the node corresponding to a supplied prefix.

nodes.name: Handling empty and absent prefixes safely
nodes.definition: Defining predictable behavior when the prefix is empty or cannot be followed in the tree.

nodes.name: Packaging frontier state as node plus path
nodes.definition: Storing the current tree node together with enough path text to reconstruct a complete suggestion.

nodes.name: Concatenating characters to reconstruct words
nodes.definition: Building complete suggestion strings by extending a prefix/path with traversed characters.

nodes.name: Appending discovered suggestions to a result list
nodes.definition: Accumulating multiple completed suggestion strings in a Python list.

nodes.name: Distinguishing return values from printed output
nodes.definition: Understanding that a function can print data without returning it, and that callers need an explicit return value.

nodes.name: Understanding FIFO queue semantics
nodes.definition: Knowing that first-in, first-out processing expands older frontier entries before newer ones.

nodes.name: Using deque append and popleft for FIFO traversal
nodes.definition: Using queue operations that implement FIFO behavior efficiently in Python.

nodes.name: Understanding LIFO stack semantics
nodes.definition: Knowing that last-in, first-out processing expands the most recently added frontier entry first.

nodes.name: Using append and pop for an explicit stack
nodes.definition: Using Python list operations to implement LIFO traversal.

nodes.name: Defining a recursion base case
nodes.definition: Providing a stopping condition so a recursive traversal terminates safely.

nodes.name: Using recursive descent and backtracking
nodes.definition: Calling a recursive traversal on children and returning to explore alternatives after a branch completes.

nodes.name: Using Python container truthiness in frontier loops
nodes.definition: Understanding that non-empty queue, stack, or heap containers are truthy and can control a `while frontier:` traversal loop.

nodes.name: Preserving a consistent child-iteration order
nodes.definition: Visiting child mappings in a chosen, repeatable order so output ordering is reproducible.

nodes.name: Accounting for stack push order in DFS
nodes.definition: Understanding that pushing several children onto a LIFO stack can reverse the order in which they are later expanded.

nodes.name: Counting repeated transition occurrences
nodes.definition: Incrementing counts when the same character transition is observed multiple times in the corpus.

nodes.name: Defining the context used for a transition frequency
nodes.definition: Choosing whether a transition count is conditioned on an immediate predecessor or a longer prefix context.

nodes.name: Converting frequency to inverse cost
nodes.definition: Applying an inverse relationship such as cost = 1/frequency so higher-frequency transitions receive lower costs.

nodes.name: Summing transition costs into a path cost
nodes.definition: Adding each new transition cost to the cost accumulated along the current candidate path.

nodes.name: Understanding min-priority-queue semantics
nodes.definition: Knowing that a min-heap or priority queue removes the frontier entry with the smallest priority value first.

nodes.name: Building heap entries with safe tie-breaking
nodes.definition: Including a deterministic secondary value when equal priorities might otherwise force Python to compare non-orderable objects.

nodes.name: Distinguishing edge cost from cumulative path cost
nodes.definition: Recognizing that UCS prioritizes total path cost rather than only the cost of the newest transition.

nodes.name: Separating occurrence counts from unique output policy
nodes.definition: Distinguishing how repeated corpus words affect frequency statistics from whether the same suggestion should be emitted more than once.

nodes.name: Understanding Python dictionary iteration order
nodes.definition: Knowing that modern Python dictionaries preserve insertion order and that this can influence deterministic traversal output.

nodes.name: Avoiding post-search sorting when algorithm order matters
nodes.definition: Recognizing that sorting a finished suggestion list can destroy the traversal order produced by BFS, DFS, or UCS.

nodes.name: Constructing a tiny controlled test corpus
nodes.definition: Creating a small set of words whose expected tree and search outputs can be reasoned about manually.

nodes.name: Manually deriving the expected prefix tree
nodes.definition: Drawing or tracing the expected nodes, branches, and terminal markers for a small word set.

nodes.name: Manually tracing frontier expansion steps
nodes.definition: Simulating queue, stack, or priority-queue contents step by step to predict search behavior.

nodes.name: Comparing expected and actual outputs
nodes.definition: Checking generated suggestions and order against a manually reasoned expectation.

nodes.name: Localizing faults by pipeline stage
nodes.definition: Separating failures in parsing, tree construction, prefix lookup, traversal, cost calculation, and output collection.

nodes.name: Explaining code through data structures and invariants
nodes.definition: Describing what state is maintained, what each loop/call guarantees, and how the chosen data structure enforces the algorithm.

nodes.name: Documenting design assumptions consistently
nodes.definition: Stating choices such as duplicate handling, frequency context, traversal order, tie-breaking, and normalization and using them consistently.

nodes.name: Connecting the intended search method to application flow
nodes.definition: Ensuring the caller or GUI invokes the implemented BFS, DFS, or UCS method rather than an old placeholder or random method.

nodes.name: Recognizing when a visited set is unnecessary in a tree
nodes.definition: Understanding that a true prefix tree has unique parent paths and no cycles, unlike a general graph with repeated states.

nodes.name: Using case conversion consistently in string comparison
nodes.definition: Understanding operations such as lowercasing and applying the same conversion to both stored words and queried prefixes when normalization is chosen.

nodes.name: Recognizing punctuation and symbols during token processing
nodes.definition: Identifying non-letter characters in parsed tokens so an implementation can consistently keep, remove, or otherwise handle them.

nodes.name: Defining deterministic equal-priority behavior
nodes.definition: Choosing a reproducible rule for ordering frontier entries that have equal UCS costs.

nodes.name: Distinguishing the call stack from an explicit DFS stack
nodes.definition: Recognizing that recursive DFS stores pending work in function calls while iterative DFS stores it in an explicit data structure.

nodes.name: Relating BFS depth to shorter completions
nodes.definition: Understanding that level-order expansion reaches shallower terminal nodes before deeper ones, subject to same-depth child order.

nodes.name: Relating high frequency to lower UCS priority cost
nodes.definition: Understanding why inverse-frequency costs make common transitions comparatively cheaper and therefore earlier candidates for UCS expansion.

nodes.name: Relating same-depth output order to child order
nodes.definition: Understanding that BFS order among suggestions at the same depth depends on the order children are enqueued.

nodes.name: Relating DFS output to branch-first exploration
nodes.definition: Understanding that DFS may return a deep completion before shallower completions in sibling branches because it follows one branch before backtracking.

The prefix-tree representation provides the concrete state space used by the autocomplete search model.
Recognizing terminal entries as goals supports understanding why multiple goal states can be collected.
A student must understand shared-prefix representation before accurately tracing the constructed tree.
Incorrect terminal representation is a common cause of missing suggestions.
Incorrect prefix-endpoint lookup is a common cause of missing suggestions.
Correct FIFO frontier policy underlies breadth-first ordering.
Correct LIFO/recursion frontier policy underlies depth-first behavior.
Priority-based frontier policy underlies UCS lowest-cost expansion.
Understanding BFS ordering helps implement the corresponding queue traversal correctly.
Understanding DFS behavior helps implement recursive depth-first traversal correctly.
Understanding DFS behavior helps implement explicit-stack traversal correctly.
Comparing recursive and stack DFS helps explain DFS implementation choices.
Child traversal order directly affects the suggestion order that must be preserved.
Priority-queue implementation details directly inform diagnosis of UCS ordering and tie errors.
Preserving algorithm order helps distinguish genuine traversal differences from accidental reordering.
Controlled testing provides evidence for localizing implementation faults.
Output-list comparison provides evidence for informal judgments about suggestion usefulness.
Clear implementation explanations require assumptions to be stated explicitly and consistently.
Explaining construction logic is one part of explaining the overall implementation.
Explaining BFS logic is one part of explaining the overall implementation.
Explaining DFS logic is one part of explaining the overall implementation.
Explaining UCS logic is one part of explaining the overall implementation.
Consistent implementation assumptions support a coherent written justification.
Normalization choices must be integrated into the overall consistency policy.
Punctuation handling choices must be integrated into the overall consistency policy.
Understanding tree-search properties supports the overall tree-search framing.
